newsitem.title: UK: United News shares down on bond issue.
newsitem.headline: United News shares down on bond issue.

text.p: Shares in United News & Media Plc dropped on Thursday after the company said it was raising 180 million stg through an issue of convertible bonds, sparking talk that the company may be poised for another acquisition.
The stock was down 10-1/2p at 686-1/2 by 1014 GMT, reversing the bulk of yesterday's gain on the back of an upbeat trading statement from local newspaper publisher Southnews Plc.
The bonds are convertible into United News shares at a rate to be set at between 14 and 18 percent above the mid-market share price at any time up to today's close.

Analysts said the move would help cut the cost of United News borrowings but was effectively a disguised rights issue that could could spark renewed speculation about further takeover activity by the acquisitive group.
United paid 592.5 million stg for exhibitions organiser Blenheim Group Plc earlier this year and holds a 20 percent stake in HTV Plc, up 1-1/2p at 357-1/2.
There is also speculation that United is poised to announce the purchase of privately-owned West Country Television for between 75 million stg and 85 million.
"They are under no financial pressure," said Louise Barton, analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite, "this is just a way of bringing in some more funds and giving them a bit more leverage."
"My feeling is they are not about to go for HTV... but it (the bond issue) might make the market a bit wary that they are about to do so," Barton said.
A spokesman for United News said the company declined comment on market speculation. No-one at West Country was immediately available for comment.
